revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Overtime Hours Limit
revealWordProblem.text: Detective Chen's team can use at most 40 hours of overtime this week to close the case. So far the team has logged 26 hours. Write an inequality for the additional overtime hours t the team can still use, solve it, and graph the solution set on a number line.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Write 26 + t ≤ 40. Subtracting 26 gives t ≤ 14. Additional overtime hours cannot be negative, so the contextual solution is 0 ≤ t ≤ 14. The team can use up to 14 more hours, including fractional hours if permitted. To graph the inequality alone, use a closed circle at 14 and shade left. For this situation, keep only the segment from 0 to 14, with closed endpoints.

questions.stem: A museum has some paintings. After adding 12, they have 45. Which equation models this?
questions.explanation: 'Adding 12' to the original number gives 45: p + 12 = 45. Solve: p = 33.
choiceFeedback: Subtracting says the museum LOST paintings, but 12 were ADDED to what they had. Choose the operation that matches 'after adding 12.'
12p means 12 groups of p, which is multiplication. Re-read what actually happened to the paintings the museum already had.
Dividing would split the paintings into 12 equal groups. The museum did something different with the 12.
hints: The museum STARTS with an unknown number of paintings p, then 12 more are ADDED to reach 45.
'Adding 12' means the model joins p and 12 with a plus sign, and the total 45 goes after the equals sign.
Write the story in order: p, plus 12, equals 45. Which choice matches without switching the operation?
questions.stemEs: Un museo tiene algunas pinturas. Después de agregar 12, tiene 45. ¿Qué ecuación representa esta situación?
questions.explanationEs: «Agregar 12» al número original da 45: p + 12 = 45. Resuelve: p = 33.
hintsEs: El museo EMPIEZA con un número desconocido de cuadros p y luego se AGREGAN 12 más para llegar a 45.
'Agregar 12' significa que el modelo une p y 12 con un signo más, y el total 45 va después del signo igual.
Escribe la historia en orden: p, más 12, es igual a 45. ¿Qué opción coincide sin cambiar la operación?

questions.stem: A detective needs more than 8 hours to finish the investigation. She has already worked 3 hours. Which inequality represents the additional hours h she needs?
questions.explanation: 3 hours plus additional hours h must be more than 8: 3 + h > 8. Solve: h > 5.
choiceFeedback: The equals sign pins her total to EXACTLY 8 hours, but she needs more than 8. Keep the total 3 + h and swap in the comparison the story demands.
This compares the extra hours to 3, but 3 is the time already worked, not the goal. It is the total of both amounts that has to pass 8.
The 8 and the 3 have swapped jobs here. 8 is the total she must go past, and 3 is what she has already finished.
hints: There are two time pieces: the 3 hours already worked and the extra hours h. Together they must pass 8 hours.
'More than 8' means the TOTAL of 3 + h sits on the big side of a strict inequality — not an equals sign.
Combine first: 3 + h. Then compare that total to 8 using the strict 'more than' symbol. Which choice is built that way?
questions.stemEs: Una detective necesita más de 8 horas para terminar la investigación. Ya trabajó 3 horas. ¿Qué desigualdad representa las horas adicionales h que necesita?
questions.explanationEs: 3 horas más las horas adicionales h deben ser más de 8: 3 + h > 8. Resuelve: h > 5.
hintsEs: Hay dos partes de tiempo: las 3 horas ya trabajadas y las horas extra h. Juntas deben pasar de 8 horas.
'Más de 8' significa que el TOTAL de 3 + h queda del lado grande de una desigualdad estricta, no de un signo igual.
Combina primero: 3 + h. Luego compara ese total con 8 usando el símbolo estricto de 'más de'. ¿Qué opción está armada así?

questions.stem: Which model is correct for: 'A number divided by 6 equals 7'?
questions.explanation: Divided by 6 is n / 6. Equals 7 means = 7. So n / 6 = 7.
choiceFeedback: That shows subtracting 6. The words say divided by 6.
hints: Spot the operation phrase: 'divided by 6'. That phrase gives you the symbol between n and 6.
Keep the sentence order — the number n comes first, then the division by 6, then 'equals 7'.
Write n / 6 on the left and 7 on the right. Which choice shows division rather than multiplying or adding 6?
questions.stemEs: ¿Qué modelo es correcto para: 'Un número dividido entre 6 es igual a 7'?
questions.explanationEs: Dividido entre 6 es n / 6. Es igual a 7 significa = 7. Entonces n / 6 = 7.
hintsEs: Identifica la frase de operación: 'dividido entre 6'. Esa frase te da el símbolo entre n y 6.
Conserva el orden de la oración: el número n va primero, luego la división entre 6 y luego 'es igual a 7'.
Escribe n / 6 a la izquierda y 7 a la derecha. ¿Qué opción muestra división en vez de multiplicar o sumar 6?

reviewHighlights.rule: Modeling Real-World Scenarios with Equations & Inequalities
steps: 1. Define the variable and units in the scenario
3. Write the algebraic model, solve with inverse operations, and check in context
reviewHighlights.watchOut: A common mistake in Equations and Inequalities Problem Solving is matching the wrong model to a key phrase. For 'the getaway car held no more than 6 bags,' students often write the equation b = 6 instead of the inequality b ≤ 6, because they see one number and assume it must be exact. The same mistake happens in reverse: for 'the reward split equally among 5 people gave each $40,' students sometimes write the inequality 5p ≥ 40 instead of the equation 5p = 40, because 'split equally' sounds like it could mean a range. Before you submit, ask: does this phrase give one exact value (equation, =) or a limit/range (inequality, <, >, ≤, ≥)?

level1.stem: A total divided equally among 2 people gave each person $35. What was the total?
level1.stemEs: Un total repartido por igual entre 2 personas le dio $35 a cada persona. ¿Cuál era el total?
hints: Write t ÷ 2 = 35. Multiply both sides by 2.
hintsEs: Escribe t ÷ 2 = 35. Multiplica los dos lados por 2.
level1.explanation: Write the equation: t ÷ 2 = 35 Multiply both sides by 2: t = 35 × 2 = 70
level1.explanationEs: Escribe la ecuación: t ÷ 2 = 35 Multiplica los dos lados por 2: t = 35 × 2 = 70

level1.stem: A cup holds at most 8 ounces. It has 5 ounces of juice. How many more ounces can you add at most?
level1.stemEs: Un vaso lleva como máximo 8 onzas. Tiene 5 onzas de jugo. ¿Cuántas onzas más puedes agregar como máximo?
hints: "At most" is a limit. Write 5 + j ≤ 8.
hintsEs: «Como máximo» es un límite. Escribe 5 + j ≤ 8.
level1.explanation: Write the inequality: 5 + j ≤ 8 Subtract 5 from both sides: 8 − 5 = 3 → j ≤ 3
level1.explanationEs: Escribe la desigualdad: 5 + j ≤ 8 Resta 5 en los dos lados: 8 − 5 = 3 → j ≤ 3

level1.stem: A total divided equally among 6 people gave each person $9. What was the total?
level1.stemEs: Un total repartido por igual entre 6 personas le dio $9 a cada persona. ¿Cuál era el total?
hints: Write t ÷ 6 = 9. Multiply both sides by 6.
hintsEs: Escribe t ÷ 6 = 9. Multiplica los dos lados por 6.
level1.explanation: Write the equation: t ÷ 6 = 9 Multiply both sides by 6: t = 9 × 6 = 54
level1.explanationEs: Escribe la ecuación: t ÷ 6 = 9 Multiplica los dos lados por 6: t = 9 × 6 = 54

level1.stem: A shelf had some books. Then 9 more books were added. Now there are 25 books. Write and solve an equation. How many books were there at first?
level1.stemEs: Un estante tenía algunos libros. Luego se pusieron 9 libros más. Ahora hay 25 libros. Escribe y resuelve una ecuación. ¿Cuántos libros había al principio?
hints: There is one exact total, so use an equation. Write b + 9 = 25.
hintsEs: Hay un solo total exacto, así que usa una ecuación. Escribe b + 9 = 25.
level1.explanation: Write the equation: b + 9 = 25 Subtract 9 from both sides: b = 25 − 9 = 16 Check it: 16 + 9 = 25 ✓
level1.explanationEs: Escribe la ecuación: b + 9 = 25 Resta 9 en los dos lados: b = 25 − 9 = 16 Compruébalo: 16 + 9 = 25 ✓

level1.stem: A total divided equally among 6 people gave each person $42. What was the total?
level1.stemEs: Un total repartido por igual entre 6 personas le dio $42 a cada persona. ¿Cuál era el total?
hints: Each person got an exact amount. Write t ÷ 6 = 42. Multiply both sides by 6.
hintsEs: Cada persona recibió una cantidad exacta. Escribe t ÷ 6 = 42. Multiplica los dos lados por 6.
level1.explanation: Write the equation: t ÷ 6 = 42 Multiply both sides by 6: t = 42 × 6 = 252 Check it: 252 ÷ 6 = 42 ✓
level1.explanationEs: Escribe la ecuación: t ÷ 6 = 42 Multiplica los dos lados por 6: t = 42 × 6 = 252 Compruébalo: 252 ÷ 6 = 42 ✓

level2.stem: Which situation needs an inequality, not an equation?
level2.stemEs: ¿Qué situación necesita una desigualdad y no una ecuación?
hints: Look for limit words like "at most," "at least," or "no more than."
hintsEs: Busca palabras de límite como «como máximo», «al menos» o «no más de».
level2.explanation: Look for limit words: no more than 12 → a ≤ 12 The other stories have exact amounts: exactly, equally, costs → =
level2.explanationEs: Busca palabras de límite: no más de 12 → a ≤ 12 Las otras historias tienen cantidades exactas: exactamente, por igual, cuesta → =
choices: A bag can hold no more than 12 apples.
Each of 3 boxes holds exactly 12 eggs.
12 cookies were shared equally by 4 kids.
choicesEs: Una bolsa puede llevar no más de 12 manzanas.
Cada una de 3 cajas lleva exactamente 12 huevos.
12 galletas se repartieron por igual entre 4 niños.
choiceFeedback: "Exactly 12" is one exact amount, so it needs an equation.
Shared equally gives one exact share, so it needs an equation.
$6 is one exact price, so it needs an equation.

level2.stem: Each shelf holds 18 books. A library has 250 books. Write and solve an inequality. How many shelves are needed?
level2.stemEs: Cada estante lleva 18 libros. Una biblioteca tiene 250 libros. Escribe y resuelve una desigualdad. ¿Cuántos estantes se necesitan?
hints: The shelves must hold at least 250 books. Write 18s ≥ 250.
hintsEs: Los estantes deben llevar al menos 250 libros. Escribe 18s ≥ 250.
level2.explanation: Write the inequality: 18s ≥ 250 Divide both sides by 18: s ≥ 250 ÷ 18 → s ≥ 13.8… Check whole shelves: 18 × 13 = 234 ✗; 18 × 14 = 252 ✓
level2.explanationEs: Escribe la desigualdad: 18s ≥ 250 Divide los dos lados entre 18: s ≥ 250 ÷ 18 → s ≥ 13.8… Comprueba estantes enteros: 18 × 13 = 234 ✗; 18 × 14 = 252 ✓

level2.stem: A total divided equally among 7 people gave each person $11. What was the total?
level2.stemEs: Un total repartido por igual entre 7 personas le dio $11 a cada persona. ¿Cuál era el total?
hints: Write t ÷ 7 = 11. Multiply both sides by 7.
hintsEs: Escribe t ÷ 7 = 11. Multiplica los dos lados por 7.
level2.explanation: Write the equation: t ÷ 7 = 11 Multiply both sides by 7: t = 11 × 7 = 77
level2.explanationEs: Escribe la ecuación: t ÷ 7 = 11 Multiplica los dos lados por 7: t = 11 × 7 = 77

level2.stem: Tickets cost $7.50 each. Ray has $40. Write and solve an inequality. What is the greatest number of tickets he can buy?
level2.stemEs: Los boletos cuestan $7.50 cada uno. Ray tiene $40. Escribe y resuelve una desigualdad. ¿Cuál es el mayor número de boletos que puede comprar?
hints: Ray cannot spend more than $40. Write 7.50t ≤ 40.
hintsEs: Ray no puede gastar más de $40. Escribe 7.50t ≤ 40.
level2.explanation: Write the inequality: 7.50t ≤ 40 Divide both sides by 7.50: t ≤ 40 ÷ 7.50 → t ≤ 5.3… Check whole tickets: 7.50 × 5 = 37.50 ✓; 7.50 × 6 = 45 ✗
level2.explanationEs: Escribe la desigualdad: 7.50t ≤ 40 Divide los dos lados entre 7.50: t ≤ 40 ÷ 7.50 → t ≤ 5.3… Comprueba boletos enteros: 7.50 × 5 = 37.50 ✓; 7.50 × 6 = 45 ✗

level2.stem: A suitcase can weigh at most 50 pounds. It has 34 pounds of clothes in it. Write and solve a model. How many more pounds can you add at most?
level2.stemEs: Una maleta puede pesar como máximo 50 libras. Tiene 34 libras de ropa. Escribe y resuelve un modelo. ¿Cuántas libras más puedes agregar como máximo?
hints: "At most" is a limit. Write 34 + w ≤ 50.
hintsEs: «Como máximo» es un límite. Escribe 34 + w ≤ 50.
level2.explanation: Write the inequality: 34 + w ≤ 50 Subtract 34 from both sides: 50 − 34 = 16 → w ≤ 16
level2.explanationEs: Escribe la desigualdad: 34 + w ≤ 50 Resta 34 en los dos lados: 50 − 34 = 16 → w ≤ 16

level3.stem: A school van can carry at most 14 passengers. There are already 9 passengers on board. Let p be the number of additional passengers who can get on. Which inequality models this situation?
choiceFeedback: This demands at least 14, which would let the van overfill. 'At most' caps the total.
This forbids a full van of exactly 14. 'At most 14' allows 14.
This subtracts the riders already aboard. They add to the total, so 9 plus p.
level3.explanation: The 9 passengers already on board plus the p additional passengers make up the total. The phrase 'at most 14' means that total may reach 14 but cannot pass it, so the model is 9 + p ≤ 14.

level3.stem: A class needs at least $300 for a trip. They earn $12 for each car wash. Kim writes 12c = 300. Lee writes 12c ≥ 300. What is the least number of car washes they need?
level3.stemEs: Una clase necesita al menos $300 para una excursión. Gana $12 por cada carro que lava. Kim escribe 12c = 300. Lee escribe 12c ≥ 300. ¿Cuál es el menor número de carros que deben lavar?
hints: Solve 12c ≥ 300. Is the boundary included?
hintsEs: Resuelve 12c ≥ 300. ¿Está incluido el límite?
level3.explanation: Divide both sides by 12: 300 ÷ 12 = 25 → c ≥ 25 Check the boundary: 12 × 25 = 300 → 300 ≥ 300 ✓
level3.explanationEs: Divide los dos lados entre 12: 300 ÷ 12 = 25 → c ≥ 25 Comprueba el límite: 12 × 25 = 300 → 300 ≥ 300 ✓

level3.stem: A box holds 24 cans. A store has 270 cans to pack. Write and solve an inequality. How many boxes are needed?
level3.stemEs: Una caja lleva 24 latas. Una tienda tiene 270 latas para empacar. Escribe y resuelve una desigualdad. ¿Cuántas cajas se necesitan?
hints: The boxes must hold at least 270 cans. Write 24b ≥ 270.
hintsEs: Las cajas deben llevar al menos 270 latas. Escribe 24b ≥ 270.
level3.explanation: Write the inequality: 24b ≥ 270 Divide both sides by 24: 270 ÷ 24 = 11.25 → b ≥ 11.25 Round up to whole boxes: 24 × 11 = 264 ✗; 24 × 12 = 288 ✓
level3.explanationEs: Escribe la desigualdad: 24b ≥ 270 Divide los dos lados entre 24: 270 ÷ 24 = 11.25 → b ≥ 11.25 Redondea hacia arriba a cajas enteras: 24 × 11 = 264 ✗; 24 × 12 = 288 ✓

level3.stem: A water tank holds at most 120 liters. It has 47.5 liters now. Write and solve a model. How many more liters can you add at most?
level3.stemEs: Un tanque de agua lleva como máximo 120 litros. Ahora tiene 47.5 litros. Escribe y resuelve un modelo. ¿Cuántos litros más puedes agregar como máximo?
hints: "At most" is a limit. Write 47.5 + w ≤ 120.
hintsEs: «Como máximo» es un límite. Escribe 47.5 + w ≤ 120.
level3.explanation: Write the inequality: 47.5 + w ≤ 120 Subtract 47.5 from both sides: 120 − 47.5 = 72.5 → w ≤ 72.5
level3.explanationEs: Escribe la desigualdad: 47.5 + w ≤ 120 Resta 47.5 en los dos lados: 120 − 47.5 = 72.5 → w ≤ 72.5

level3.stem: A gym charges $20 to join, plus $15 each month. Sam can spend at most $140. Write and solve an inequality. How many months can he pay for?
level3.stemEs: Un gimnasio cobra $20 de inscripción, más $15 cada mes. Sam puede gastar como máximo $140. Escribe y resuelve una desigualdad. ¿Cuántos meses puede pagar?
hints: Write 20 + 15m ≤ 140. Undo the + 20 first, then undo the × 15.
hintsEs: Escribe 20 + 15m ≤ 140. Primero deshaz el + 20 y luego deshaz el × 15.
level3.explanation: Write the inequality: 20 + 15m ≤ 140 Subtract 20 from both sides: 140 − 20 = 120 → 15m ≤ 120 Divide both sides by 15: 120 ÷ 15 = 8 → m ≤ 8
level3.explanationEs: Escribe la desigualdad: 20 + 15m ≤ 140 Resta 20 en los dos lados: 140 − 20 = 120 → 15m ≤ 120 Divide los dos lados entre 15: 120 ÷ 15 = 8 → m ≤ 8
